messages:
maria: Heads-up — customers in AP-South reporting p95 for /v1/embeddings up ~2.5x since the nightly driver + cuda rollout (~sha: b3f4a2d). Started ~02:10 UTC. Seeing error-free requests but long tail.
josh: :eyes: which hosts? graphs?
maria: ap-south-edge-*/embed route. Attached perf graph: p50 stable, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 320ms. No auth/billing errors. No change in QPS.
kevin: Any storage errors in node logs? Previously driver rollouts caused hostfs io spikes.
amanda: grabbing `iostat -x 1 5` and dmesg from a noisy host now.
amanda: ```
iostat -x 1 5
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00   75.00  1024.00  8192.00   0.00   10.00   0.45   9.01   0.50   9.46   0.20  16.5
``` 
amanda: and dmesg shows a bunch of `nvme: abort due to timeout` and `eth0: dropped packet` entries.
josh: that nvme wait pattern looks like storage-caused tail. Could be IO scheduler/cgroup change from the kernel we rolled.
kevin: which kernel + driver? last night we pushed kernel 6.5.x + nvidia 555.8 and firmware 2.3.4 as a bundle.
maria: yes, bundle id `roll-2026-03-16-22`.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot rolled out bundle roll-2026-03-16-22 to ap-south-edge (50 hosts) at 02:05 UTC.
josh: quick repro: run parallel embed requests pinned to same host while running `fio --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=64` to simulate NVMe tail. If p95 moves up, storage is the culprit.
kevin: do we have KV cache pressure evidence? If long storage latencies interleave with KV cache writes, tails go up even if GPU is fine.
amanda: fio on a test host produced 99th latency ~18ms with iodepth 64, but under embed traffic we see app-level p99 > 200ms.
maria: mitigation options: 1) rollback driver/kernel bundle to previous build (safe, but broad). 2) Move embed route traffic to eu-edge fallback (routing change). 3) Pin high-SLA customers to Dedicated pool. 4) Kernel qdisc / IOPS cgroup tweak on ap-south nodes.
josh: short term: routing fallback for customer-facing embed routes to eu-edge for affected customers. Ops can add route policy on the LB (sticky for session). Longer term: bisect kernel vs driver vs firmware.
kevin: agree. Action: amanda and infra will rollback driver on 10 canaries and run perf. If rollback reduces p95 -> we know driver/firmware. If not, check kernel config and nvme firmware.
amanda: starting canary rollback now on ap-south-edge-03..06.
amanda: deploy-bot: rollback started for hosts [ap-south-edge-03, ap-south-edge-04, ap-south-edge-05, ap-south-edge-06]
deploy-bot: rollback completed for hosts [ap-south-edge-03, ap-south-edge-04, ap-south-edge-05, ap-south-edge-06]
amanda: post-rollback p95 on canaries dropped from 320ms -> 130ms for embeds. p50 unchanged.
josh: good signal that bundle caused it. Next: schedule full rollback for the region OR patch driver. What's the customer impact window if we rollback region-wide?
maria: if we rollback region, dependency disruption minimal (short restarts). Expected recovery within 10–15 mins per node, rolling over 2 hours for 50 hosts.
kevin: check for any GPU firmware incompatibilities — rollback may require kernel module reload sequence: `modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia && modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm` — watch for OOM in pods during reload.
amanda: I'm preparing runbook and will kick full rollback on approval. Also flagging for devs: reproduce locally with `cuda 12.2 -> 13` mix and nvme stress.
maria: Scott from support reached out — will inform customers that we identified a driver-bundle regression and are rolling back; offering temporary route fallback for high-latency tasks.
oncall-bot: incident tagged SEV3 -> SEV2 due to customer impact to latency-sensitive embeddings.
kevin: follow-ups: 1) bisect driver commit between b3f4a2d and previous working sha 9a2c1ff. 2) run nvme firmware health checks across region. 3) add host-level IO limits for embed route traffic via cgroups.
josh: will create a tracing ticket to correlate per-request kernel latency with NVMe qdepth. Also add a metric alert on nvme_saturation (new gauge) to detect early.
maria: thanks team. Amanda — file postmortem once rollback completes and we have bisect result. I'll notify customers now.
amanda: rollback completed region-wide at 03:40 UTC, p95 back to ~140ms. Opening postmortem doc: /docs/incidents/9807654321-postmortem-draft
maria: :thumbsup: closing loop with support to verify customer latency improvements.
kevin: once PM is happy, schedule targeted canary for the newer driver with nvme fio tests before any large rollout.
end
